$comment: THE GUARD REGISTRY — every enforcement promise OneEngine makes.
`scripts/guards.test.mjs` reads this file. Four rules make it more than a
1. A `live` guard names an implementation AND a literal string that
implementation contains. Rename the assertion and the registry fails,
so a guard cannot quietly stop existing.
2. A `live` guard must actually RUN — reached by `pnpm engine:gate`,
`engine:test` or `engine:typecheck`. A check nobody invokes is no check.
3. Every guard names the DECISION it protects. A guard defending nothing
recorded is one whose reason is forgotten and which is then deleted as
noise by somebody who cannot see what it was for.
4. An `owed` guard names a stage, and a SHIPPED stage may owe nothing —
which is what makes the stage table in PLAN.md mean anything.
`fails` is a consequence in the world, never a restatement of the assertion:
"a tenant's records unreachable after a move", not "the key is wrong".

guards.fails: a crown of four controls at three different widths, because a button with only a glyph in it still lays out w-fit px-4
a Table.Column outside Table.Content throwing during render, so the whole screen is blank
a nav of four destinations at four widths, with the current one inheriting whichever width its own label happened to make

guards.proves: travel: the nav names one destination
guards.fails: the nav's fill and its label come from two expressions, so it highlights one destination and names another — or a closed label is removed rather than narrowed, which is five unnamed buttons to the one group the icon carries nothing for
a hero that renders at the size of the heading above it, because two roles resolved to the same size and neither looked wrong alone
a visible lattice across every light screen, drawn by the layer whose whole job is to be invisible

guards.proves: refuses a shard whose schema does not cover the tenant's apps
guards.fails: every request for one customer answering "no such table", after a move that reported success

guards.proves: refuses a shard in the wrong place, whatever else is true of it
guards.fails: a business told their customers' records stay in the EU, and a rebalance that moved them out

guards.proves: stops accepting at the ceiling, and says nothing about who is already there
guards.fails: a number an operator typed becoming an outage trigger at whatever hour it is crossed

guards.proves: counts a disabled app when deciding what a shard needs
guards.fails: records stranded by a move, readable again the day the product is switched back on — in a database that cannot read them
a document nothing links to, drifting unread until somebody quotes it back as current
a stage marked shipped with unfinished work inside it, so "shipped" stops meaning anything
a hand-typed count wrong within a week, and a document that stops being read for the parts that are right
a guard whose reason nobody can find, deleted as noise by somebody who cannot see what it was for
a contract layer that needs a binding to test, so the rules stop being provable and start being fixtures
a shared module that knows what a client is, which has stopped being shared
`engine` meaning the scene engine, the frame engine or the rendered engine, inside the thing called OneEngine
consistency that is maintained by care rather than enforced, which lasts until the first hurried screen
a bottom bar that stopped being tappable and became a menu
a mechanism built, tested and wired with nowhere a person can look — every suite green
a declared kind falling through to a text box, which looks finished and accepts anything
a switch somebody turns on that does nothing, so they stop watching the thing it promised
guards.proves: the screens show nothing the manifest does not declare

guards.fails: a concern an app can forget, forgotten invisibly — no error, no failing test, a capability that silently does not apply
an app writing the vault's own tables directly, so a fact exists with no grant, no consent record and no way to shred it
an operator console that gets slower with every shard, until the sweep it runs times out
cold start growing with the catalogue, until the catalogue that was meant to grow cannot
a suite that is wrong half the time and green every time, with the next real intermittent failure absorbed by the same line
a screen that says "you have nothing" while it is still loading, and says it again when the request failed
a confident zero on the first paint — a badge, an all-caught-up, a no-media-yet — every one of them a wrong answer wearing a loading state's excuse
a layout that jumps the moment data lands, which is worse than one that was briefly blank
a product with a dozen animation techniques and therefore no motion design, accreted one defensible animation at a time
an effect that is exported, imported, and never injected — so it has never once run, and looks exactly like a design decision
twenty screens at gap-2, gap-3, gap-4 and gap-10, each defensible, with nobody able to point at which one is wrong
an accent that is the button, the link, the nav pill and the ramp all at once — present on every screen, meaning nothing, and needing a second colour before anything can stand out
four quick-action chips 0.025 from the light page reading as smudges, while a hand-picked pair list reported the palette sound
a wrong payload becoming a production error where it had been a compile error
a declaration that has to be executed before it can be read, so every generated surface stops being derivable
one of our own rules living inside somebody else's package, re-learned from their release notes
a message switched on in the policy screen that never arrives, so people stop trusting the ones that do
somebody turning on a control that does nothing, and no longer watching for the problem it promised to solve
money taken for a capability every customer already has, failing in the generous direction so nobody reports it
somebody's health record in a product table, outside consent, outside the grant log and outside crypto-shredding
a deletion request that reports success and leaves the rows, because the sweep had nothing to follow

guards.proves: refuses a statement that would fail quietly
guards.fails: a DROP running itself on every shard at 3am because somebody edited a declaration
a generated schema built from something a request supplied, which is the injection this whole design forecloses
a manifest that can call the machinery, which is a manifest that can leave a gate out of the next handler
a customer answering on the hostname a certificate authority validates against, or on the operator's own door
a handler that runs for somebody who was never allowed to call it, because one call site forgot the check

guards.proves: answers a replay with the first answer
guards.fails: a phone that retried in a basement getting a second charge, a second notification and two of what it made once

guards.proves: records an attempt that was refused
guards.fails: an incident review asking who tried and finding silence, because only the successes were recorded
a two-step escalation: invite a second address of your own as an owner, then sign in as it

guards.proves: they claim it by signing in as it
guards.fails: anybody holding an account id adding themselves to a workspace they were never invited to

guards.proves: resolved from the roster on every request
guards.fails: a role taken away that keeps working until the person signs out, which is exactly when it matters that it does not

guards.proves: cannot be started from inside somebody else's workspace
guards.fails: somebody who followed a colleague's link being invited to start a second workspace on that workspace's own branded page
a six-digit password with unlimited attempts, and a sign-in endpoint anybody can use to mail somebody a hundred times
a control missing the focus ring, the pressed state and the keyboard behaviour, which looks fine and so survives review
a count that lands on top of the time beside it, because a positioned component written without its anchor still compiles, still renders, and still looks like a component

guards.proves: never puts a stored secret into the page
guards.fails: a live credential handed to every script in the page and to whatever the browser saved

guards.proves: draws only what this person can reach
guards.fails: a nav item that leads to a 403, which the person cannot tell from something simply broken

guards.proves: is a handful of variables and nothing else
guards.fails: a workspace able to break its own customers' screens on our infrastructure, and to make a page look like something it is not

guards.proves: holds a plan in each and pays one bill
guards.fails: a customer of two products becoming two customers - two cards, two renewal dates, two companies as far as they can tell

guards.proves: never charges more than was held
guards.fails: every unit an estimate fails to anticipate charged to a customer instead of absorbed, or absorbed silently on every call

guards.proves: refuses a second hold that the balance cannot cover
guards.fails: two concurrent calls both passing the same balance check, and a balance that went negative long after the calls that did it

guards.proves: stops writes after a week and still serves every read
guards.fails: a business locked out of its own records over an unpaid invoice, which is holding their data hostage

guards.proves: never reads a signup in progress as arrears
guards.fails: a brand-new workspace held read-only over an invoice that never existed, in its first minute

guards.proves: holds a workspace at what it was sold
guards.fails: give this workspace ten seats becoming a one-way door whose only reverse discards what they were originally sold
invented output served as fact in production, billed for, with every suite green because the suites run where mocking is correct

guards.proves: gives the credits back when the provider fails
guards.fails: a customer whose balance shrank for a call that returned nothing, with the hold never released

guards.proves: still files the row when every interruption is switched off
guards.fails: somebody who muted email having no record at all of what happened while they were not looking

guards.proves: reaches everybody who holds the key
guards.fails: a workspace that made its own role silently receiving nothing, with every dispatch reporting success against an empty audience

guards.proves: never shows one person another person's inbox
guards.fails: a workspace filter without the account, which is everybody reading everybody else's notifications
a field that looks safer than a plain column and survives an erasure - key not shredded, reads unrecorded, export unaware it exists

guards.proves: destroys the key, and then nobody can read any of it
guards.fails: telling somebody they were forgotten while a readable copy sits in a backup that already left the building

guards.proves: refuses a perfectly good grant once consent is withdrawn
guards.fails: an operator-written grant standing in for the subject's own agreement, which is a lawful-basis failure wearing an access-control shape

guards.proves: records the reads and the refusals alike
guards.fails: the question "did anybody try to look at this" answered with silence, which is the question actually asked after something goes wrong

guards.proves: refuses to reopen somebody who was erased
guards.fails: a fresh salt after a shredding, making everything written afterwards a second collection nobody agreed to

guards.proves: derives its whole surface, including what it never declared
guards.fails: a product that has to write its own router, schema, gates and audit, which is a product that can leave one of them out

guards.proves: lets a client log a set, and the coach see it
guards.fails: somebody's logbook readable by anybody in the workspace, because a handler forgot a WHERE

guards.proves: counts staff against the seats and clients against the clients
guards.fails: a studio on the smallest plan unable to add the customers it exists to serve, refused for staff seats it was not asking for
an expired session that does not look expired — every screen showing the empty state its failed load produced, and every save failing into a toast

guards.proves: doors: the Hub never classifies its own hostname
guards.fails: a page offering a control the runtime refuses, answered as a 404 with nothing on it to explain why

guards.proves: screens: every one the picker can name has a branch
guards.fails: a blank page, which is the same picture as a page that failed to load — so somebody reloads for a minute and then gives up

guards.proves: leaves nothing behind when the send failed
guards.fails: somebody locked out for a minute waiting on a code that was never delivered, told they are asking too often
a deploy reporting green while the isolate throws in its first middleware — the page still loads, because static assets never reach the worker

guards.proves: registry: apps.json names nothing under engine/
guards.fails: the framework shipping to the account a paying tenant is served from, selected by a workflow that derives its app list from a file somebody tidily added it to
one product reading another's rows, or a deploy replacing a live worker — a worker name is account-wide and provisioning finds a database by name
route precedence rather than intent deciding who answers a paying customer's own subdomain

guards.proves: refuses to serve at all when it cannot sign anything
guards.fails: every sign-in code signed with a constant anybody reading the repository already has, on a deployment where nothing looks wrong

guards.proves: curves: no screen writes its own easing or duration
guards.fails: a product where a drawer, a toast and a card each decelerate differently — nothing broken, nothing nameable, and it reads as cheap

guards.proves: keyframes: every one is switched off both ways
guards.fails: an animation that keeps running for somebody who asked it to stop, which for some people is a symptom rather than a preference

guards.proves: type: no screen picks its own size or weight
guards.fails: thirty screens each choosing a defensible heading size, and a product with no typographic system at all
a record nobody can attribute, discovered at the moment somebody needs to know who changed it

guards.proves: update: the generated edit goes through
guards.fails: an edit that passes the gate, writes an audit entry saying it happened, answers 200 — and changes nothing

guards.proves: cannot reach a record that is not the caller's
guards.fails: a guessed id from another workspace answering 200 as though the change landed

guards.proves: written string(s), all in one voice
guards.fails: a product that sounds like several products — a caption with a full stop beside four without one, a control that says Submit, an error that says Oops

guards.proves: fire on the copy they exist to catch
guards.fails: a green run that means nothing, because the checker's own rules stopped matching anything
a hairline here and a soft shadow there, read as two different kinds of thing when they are the same claim twice
cards that vanish in one theme when shadows are dropped, looking like a rendering fault rather than a decision
a ban kept in our files while the components draw their own, so the rule reads as held and is not
a palette that is entirely correct and reaches nothing, because the page is the user agent canvas and a light card comes out darker than it
a gate that silently does not apply to agents, because the MCP door ran the handler itself and the first forgotten concern is invisible
a tool hidden from the list and still callable — or a distinct refusal that confirms the name to the model that was refused it
an agent shown every tool including the refusals, taught to try them, with an audit row per call that was never going to run
a model that can invite somebody to a workspace from a sentence in a document it was asked to summarise
a role in the second product grants nothing, silently, for everybody — every suite green because every suite has one app
anybody who can edit access escalates in two steps: grant yourself the role you lack through the authority nobody bounds, then use it
a role in one product rings bells about another product's events for people who cannot even open it
money taken for a key nothing reads, discovered at the customer's first 403 weeks after the editor said saved
a purchase that sells access for ever, because a bare grant is a standing exception and the resolver is correct to honour it
two overlapping windows for one purchase, and which one the resolver reads decides what somebody paid for
a model composes or applies what a payment buys from a sentence in a document

guards.proves: draws every screen the parser can produce
guards.fails: a path the parser can produce renders a blank page, which is the same picture as a page that failed to load

guards.proves: offers a customer nothing their role cannot open
guards.fails: a customer opens Money and every call on the screen is a 403 dressed as a broken page

guards.proves: reads and writes each one back
guards.fails: a screen held in component state cannot be linked to, landed on or reloaded, and a refusal saying "read this first" has nowhere to send anybody

guards.proves: dismisses at the root and steps up everywhere else
guards.fails: two screens get the way out right by hand and the third goes home from three levels in, or a cycle makes the back button never leave

guards.proves: never claims a hub address as a product's
guards.fails: an app ships a screen under /hub, it is unreachable, and its author finds out from somebody who could not open it
the second product's packages and settings are unreachable for ever, because the route resolves whichever app is first on the tenant's list
the deployment's own console answers at a workspace's address, or admits anybody holding a session, and looks exactly like working software
a closed deployment serves right through the agent door, or an unprovisioned switch refuses every request over our own missing row
a deployment decision shipped through a product release — wrong the day the provider retires the row, and different in every app, with nothing failing
a variable nothing offers is sent to a model as a literal brace, and the answer comes back subtly wrong with nobody the wiser
the bill stops matching what anybody was shown, because the run used a different model or different words than the console reported

guards.proves: primary: every screen has at most one
guards.fails: the one thing a screen is for lands somewhere different on every screen — buried at the foot of a long list on one, pinned on the next — so somebody has to hunt for it and the product reads as assembled by different people; and a block comment written between two tags ships four lines of design rationale to production as body text

the same person is a picture in the crown, a letter in the roster and a different letter in a table — because each surface seeded a face from whatever field it happened to hold, and every one of them looks correct on its own

somebody gets a new face the day they correct the spelling of their name, and a workspace gets a new one the day it is renamed — so a picture people had learned to recognise means nothing; and a face fetched from api.dicebear.com puts a third party in the request path of every roster, unnamed on the trust screen

a product appears beside a person as a bare character somebody typed — no ground under it, a different optical weight from every face in the same bar — so a workspace with six products is six identical glyphs and the label does all the work

the ground somebody lands on is a different world from the planet in the row they pressed — because the sky's colours were re-derived by a hash of ours instead of read out of the picture, and the two agreed until one of them was edited
a workspace's sky is a different place on every reload, which nobody reports because nobody can hold two of them side by side
a full-viewport layer repaints every frame for ever on a phone — invisible on the laptop it was written on, and the first thing a reviewer blames on the device
one screen's contrast problem is fixed with a scrim, and every workspace's brand is grey behind a film nobody outside that file can see
the same world is sparse on a desktop and crowded on a phone, and whichever screen it was tuned on is the only one it looks right on
a screen derives the ground, the hero face and the density separately from one fact, and the day one of them is edited the crown wears one workspace's planet over another workspace's sky
a soft mark fills with a gradient id nothing defines — a valid SVG, a rendered page, and a family's whole atmosphere silently absent
an unfilled slot interpolates `undefined` into CSS, the browser drops that one declaration, and a four-layer ground quietly becomes three
one sky registered twice is the made-up rule coming back — a night ground turned down for light mode, which is grey every time

guards.proves: keeps a CSS custom property out of any mark
guards.fails: `var(--brand)` inside an SVG is a string rather than a colour — the mark is painted with nothing and the whole field is absent, with a valid document and no error anywhere

guards.proves: lays a lattice on whole cells
guards.fails: a cell that does not divide the tile leaves half-cells down every seam — a ruled line across the page at the one pitch the eye is best at finding, and invisible in the source
a file path inside the design system becomes public, so nothing in it can be renamed, split or folded away again
a hand-rolled dock skips the rules the declaration carries — a primary over a skeleton, over a refusal, or duplicated inside an empty state
